sentences.text: The Amazon rainforest is a type of tropical rainforest, characterized by a closed and continuous tree canopy, with moisture-dependent vegetation, and a diverse array of plant and animal species.
It has a warm and wet climate, with no substantial dry season, and plays a significant role in mitigating global warming.
The Amazon rainforest has seen a surge in fires, which can be devastating to the ecosystem, with over 80,000 fires reported in 2019, a 77% increase from the previous year.
Fires normally occur around the dry season as slash-and-burn methods are used to clear the forest, leading to deforestation and habitat loss.

The fate of the Amazon rainforest is a concern, as it is estimated that over 40% of all biotic species are indigenous to the rainforests, and the loss of this ecosystem could have severe consequences for the environment.

The Amazon rainforest is a moist broadleaf tropical rainforest, spanning over 7 million km2, and is home to many species of plants, insects, and microorganisms, making it a significant source of natural medicines.
The conservation of the Amazon rainforest is crucial, and efforts are being made to protect this vital ecosystem.
